name: Text Embeddings by Weakly-Supervised Contrastive Pre-training (E5)
problem: Embedding models supervised on a single task or a small labelled set failed to generalise to retrieval.
mechanism: Trains a BERT-family encoder contrastively against a curated large-scale text PAIR dataset (CCPairs) with weak supervision - the positive signal is that two texts co-occur, not a human relevance label. Adds an average-pooling layer for the embedding.
speedup_reported: E5 is the first model to beat the BM25 baseline zero-shot on the BEIR retrieval benchmark without labelled data; fine-tuned it beats MTEB-best models using 40x fewer parameters. Quality claims on MTEB/BEIR; no latency or hardware disclosure.
notes: VENUE: Semantic Scholar records this title's venue as arXiv.org only, and crossref finds no proceedings entry - cited here as a preprint rather than guessed into ACL/EMNLP. The practical reason E5 and its descendants are everywhere: a single 110-330M encoder serving retrieval, classification and clustering beats much larger alternatives, so the cheapest way to add embeddings to a system is to run one of these rather than an LLM. That is exactly the trade the 'Embedder's Dilemma' paper quantifies.
